rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one stepped compact mass with a clear primary figure, so it is not rejected for view inconsistency or colliding solids. The thin green parcel is respected by the footprint and the building remains inside the boundary. The blue access edge is answered only modestly: there is some apparent ground differentiation, but the response is weaker than ideal and the void/public threshold remains underdeveloped. Still, the form is legible, repairable, and not merely a generic box. For a neighborhood-living program, the object can plausibly support mixed-use capacity, though it currently leans more toward a compact stepped object than an explicitly active street-building section. The main next move is to strengthen the access-side carve/court while preserving the dominant stepped gesture.
